default: INTEGER autoincrement - `id Int @id @default(autoincrement())`. Fast, small indexes; right for most tables.
uuid: For a UUID PK, declare `id String @id @default(uuid())` in schema.prisma (or use the `+uuid` table flag in shorthand schema). The framework emits a TEXT PK, generates a v4 UUID server-side on INSERT, returns the real UUID from POST (not a rowid), and makes FKs that reference the table TEXT automatically. Fully supported end-to-end.
uuid_upgrade: Prisma uuid() uses the same version-4/variant-correct SQLite expression as +uuid. For existing tables, single CRUD create, batch, transaction, ingest and Mode A import supply omitted UUID defaults when the published Prisma declaration is uuid() and the physical default is the known generated expression. Stored IDs, explicit SQL IDs, explicit non-PK values/nulls, custom SQL defaults and cuid() are stored as given; generic CRUD protects primary keys. No table rebuild is performed. Raw SQL inserts (including flows/commands/restore) into existing tables use the table's stored column default: use an explicit v4 UUID expression/value or migrate that default deliberately. SQL-only schemas require the same explicit migration; the framework does not infer uuid() from an arbitrary TEXT key.
canonical_ids: A request addresses a row by the exact text of its id. For an integer key that is the plain decimal form: /api/notes/1, never /api/notes/01, /1.0, /+1, /1e0 or an id with surrounding spaces - SQLite would match those to row 1 by value, while locks, record shares, audit rows and approvals are keyed by the id text. A non-canonical id is treated as a row that does not exist: 404 on read, update, delete, workflow transitions, lock, versions/revert and approvals, 403 on share, 404 `not found or not authorized` from /api/_transaction, skipped by batch, and refused for signed-URL records. Text keys (UUIDs, slugs) are compared exactly. Send the id the API returned, unchanged.
when: Use UUID for ids exposed externally (shareable links, public tokens, cross-system integration) or where sequential-integer ids would leak row counts / invite enumeration. Otherwise INTEGER. A UUID is unguessability/defense-in-depth - owner/group access scoping is still the real authorization control, not the id type. Full authoring detail: docs/agent/build.md → schema.prisma → Primary keys.
